title: A 28nm Multimode Multiband RF Transceiver with Harmonic-Rejection TX and Spur-Avoidance RX Supporting LTE Cat1bis
problem: Cellular IoT applications (LTE Cat1bis) demand cost-effective RF transceivers supporting diverse data rates and frequency bands. Die size, packaging, and bill-of-materials (BoM) cost are critical adoption barriers. Traditional transceivers incur high silicon area overhead for multi-band support and complex TX/RX filtering.
motivation: IoT adoption (asset tracking, POS, wearables) is heavily cost-driven; integrated multimode/multiband transceivers must minimize area and component count while supporting eDRX and PSM power-save modes.
method: A 28nm CMOS multimode multiband RF transceiver integrates harmonic-rejection transmitter architecture reducing external filter requirements and spur-avoidance RX front-end enabling simpler filtering. Multiband support via tunable filtering and integrated LNA/mixer/IF stages minimize external components while supporting LTE Cat1bis protocols.
key_novelty: Harmonic-rejection TX combined with spur-avoidance RX in single integrated transceiver reducing BoM and die area for cost-sensitive IoT applications.
contributions: Harmonic-rejection TX architecture reducing external harmonic filter requirements
Spur-avoidance RX front-end enabling simpler integrated filtering
Multimode/multiband support (diverse IoT applications) in single die
Reduced BoM and form factor enabling competitive IoT device positioning
baselines: Traditional multi-band transceivers with external filtering
primary_theme: Integrated IoT RF transceiver with harmonic-rejection TX and spur-avoidance RX
